neighbours.label: A diagnostic test or work-up being ordered or listed in a medical text (doctor may order ⟦an⟧ MRI, ⟦serial⟧ ECG, ⟦complete⟧ blood count, initial ⟦investigations⟧)
fire: If the cough lasts more than three weeks, your doctor may order a chest X-ray.
The emergency team requested an ECG, a full blood count and a troponin level.
To rule out a clot, the physician will arrange an ultrasound scan of the leg.
Routine screening includes a lipid panel, a fasting glucose test and a urinalysis.
Because the headaches were getting worse, the neurologist ordered an MRI of the brain.
Your vet may recommend a blood profile and an abdominal X-ray before surgery.
At the first visit the midwife will take a urine sample and order a blood test.
When the fever did not settle, further investigations included a CT scan and blood cultures.
quiet: If the cough lasts more than three weeks, your doctor may suggest a cough syrup.
The emergency team gave oxygen, a dose of aspirin and a nitrate spray.
To prevent a clot, the physician will prescribe a blood thinner for the leg.
Routine advice includes a balanced diet, a daily walk and enough sleep.
Because the headaches were getting worse, the neurologist prescribed a stronger tablet.
Your vet may recommend a special diet and a short rest before surgery.
At the first visit the midwife will give a leaflet and suggest a vitamin supplement.
When the fever did not settle, further treatment included a second antibiotic and fluids.

notes: Card: ' an' after 'your doctor may also order', ' serial' ECG, ' investigations', ' tests', ' complete' blood count. Probes: order an X-ray 0.63, radiograph / serial troponins / complete blood count 0.79, a urinalysis and an ultrasound 0.56, investigations / further tests 0.41; prescribe an antibiotic 0.11, a manager ordering a shipment 0.23, school tests 0.01. So it is the diagnostic work-up, not 'order an' and not 'tests' alone.
